title: Grateful Dead Live at Stanley Theatre on 1972-09-28

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard stereo mix captures a high‑energy 1972 second set with smoking “He’s Gone”, “The Other One” and classic NFA sandwich.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its superb stereo soundboard quality and dynamic mix, while the performance shines with a rousing second set that features standout renditions of He’s Gone, The Other One (with Phil’s epic bass solo), Wharf Rat, Sugar Magnolia and a classic Not Fade Away sandwich. Reviewers note tight transitions, high energy and memorable contributions from Jerry, Phil, Keith and Donna.

ai_rating.rationale: All three detailed reviews are highly positive (4‑5 stars), highlighting both an excellent soundboard recording and a top‑tier musical performance with multiple standout moments.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stereo mix described as superb, clear, with great dynamics; no major flaws mentioned. Keith’s synth is low in the mix but appropriate to the sound.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set flows tightly from a rousing Bertha/Good Shepherd tease into Brokedown Palace, Teddy Bear Picnic, Me & My Uncle, Ramble on Rose, El Paso, then launches into He's Gone → Phil's bass solo → The Other One with spacey jams before closing with Wharf Rat, Sugar Magnolia and the classic Not Fade Away sandwich.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Delivers ferocious leads and a St. Stephen tease; guitar tone praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Stars on El Paso and delivers an impressive early‑song bass solo that sets up The Other One; described as “bombing”.
band_member_comments.Bob: Strong vocal presence, especially on the opening verse of The Other One.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith contributes synth textures that add a spacey vibe (low in mix but effective). Donna’s backing vocals are highlighted on Greatest and He's Gone.
band_member_comments.Drums: Funky drumming noted, with Bill Kreutzmann driving the groove during The Other One and other jams.
